name: Industry Enhancements
summary: Recipe figures, stat totals/columns, cargo filter, inactive workers, worker status, expansion, plots
description:
Corrects the production figures industries show when they have more than one recipe, such as the canning factory (fish or meat, each with sheet metal), shows which workers don't count for an industry's worker boost and what each worker is doing, filters the statistics Industries tab by cargo, marks industries that can't expand, gives the Industries tab columns for comparing industries and shows when raw producers next try to grow. Each feature can be turned off in the mod's Settings (the gear next to the mod when choosing a game's mods). Settings also has a Logging switch, off by default, that writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt) for bug reports.

Recipe Figures: the industry window's Production card shows one row per recipe, with each cargo's current and maximum consumption or production per year. The game shows the first recipe's figures again on later rows, so the canning factory's meat row repeats the fish figures. With this mod every row shows its own cargos' figures; a cargo two recipes share, such as sheet metal, shows the industry's total on both rows.

Statistics Totals: the statistics window's Industries tab counts each cargo once in its Input and Output columns. The game counts a cargo once per recipe that uses it, and takes later recipes' figures from the first. Workload compares the input with what the largest recipe takes when it runs all the time, since an industry runs one recipe at a time. Industries with one recipe and no booster show the same figures as before.

Cargo Filter: the statistics window's Industries tab gets a cargo list next to the eye. Pick a cargo to see only the industries that need it, use it as a booster or make it; All Cargo shows them all again. It works together with the eye and the search, and keeps your choice until you quit the game.

Inactive Workers: an industry's worker boost counts only workers who arrived by your lines within the last 2 years. The booster card shows their count and lists only them, so workers who walk, drive or haven't come by line for 2 years appear nowhere. With this mod the count adds them in brackets: 11 (8)/10 means 11 came by line, 8 more work there, and 10 are needed for the boost. The expanded worker list shows them below the others at 0 %, and every row shows how the worker gets to work (walking, car or lines), or a button to the new workplace of a worker who now works elsewhere, and a button that opens the worker's home (with Worker Status on, the list shows Worker Status's columns instead). This also applies to the perk window's workers. The statistics window's Industries tab shows the same count in its Workplaces column, with the filled workplaces in the tooltip.

Worker Status: the booster card's worker list shows what each worker is doing right now: at home, shopping or at work (green), walking, driving, waiting at a stop for a bus, tram, train, ship or aircraft (a stopwatch and the line's vehicle), or riding one, with a dot in the line's colour. Point at it for the line, the stop and where they get off; click it to open the worker's window. The next columns show where the current trip goes (click to open that building; a grey workplace for a worker who now works elsewhere), how many days the worker has been in that state (a wait over 30 days in red, since it makes people unhappy; "<1 d" under a day; "12 d+" when the list didn't see the state begin, "–" while that is under a day), the worker's happiness (the person window's happy or sad face and a %, with whether it is rising or falling on hover), the distance to the worker's home town (point at it for the town, click it to open the home; sort by it to see who comes from the same town), and Time Left as a % from red (0 %) to green (100 %). The worker's name is the location button's tooltip. The list starts with the workers on their way to work here, the longest under way first, and every column can be sorted.

Blocked Expansion: when an industry can't grow because something is in the way, its window says "Industry is blocked from further expansion.", but the statistics window shows nothing. With this mod the Industries tab's Problems column marks such an industry with the problem icon. Hover it for the industry window's message, click it to open the industry, which shows the blocked area on the map, and sort by the column to list them together. The mark goes away once the way is clear, just as the industry window's message does.

Industry Columns: the statistics window's Industries tab gets columns for comparing industries: Name, Problems, Plots, Recipe In, Recipe Out, Workload, Input, Output, Shipment, Boosters and Workplaces. Plots shows a raw producer's plots built of the most it may have (5/8), so you can find the ones that can grow largest. Recipe In and Recipe Out show each recipe's input and output cargos a year without boosts, a line per recipe in the same order as Input and Output, and sort by the largest. Workload adds what the boosts on now add in green, so Input is about Recipe In × Workload × (1 + boost). Input, Output and Shipment show an icon and amount per cargo and sort by the sum. Boosters shows how much faster each cargo booster makes production, in green while it is on. Workplaces adds the worker boost the same way after the worker count. Both sort the boosts that are on first, then by how much they add. Requirements is left out, since Input shows the same cargos.

Plot Growth: a raw producer (mine, farm, forest, well…) grows by one plot at a time, which raises its output. The game tries every half year, with a chance from how well it produces and how much of its output your lines ship: none at 25 % or less, sure from 75 %. The industry window's Production card doesn't say any of this. With this mod the row under the plots icon shows the plots built of the most the industry may have (15/20) and when the next try comes (43 days): green when it will succeed, yellow when it may, grey when it can't, also while the industry is blocked from further expansion (the try adds no plot unless the way is clear by then). Hover it for the chance and what it is made of. The statistics window's Plots column (Industry Columns) shows the same.

params.name: Recipe Figures
params.tooltip: In an industry's Production card, every recipe row shows its own cargos' figures (stock repeats the first recipe's); a cargo two recipes share shows its total.

params.name: Plot Growth
params.tooltip: The industry window's Production card shows under a raw producer's plots the most it may have and when the game next tries to add a plot (green sure, yellow maybe, grey no chance or blocked from further expansion).

params.name: Inactive Workers
params.tooltip: The booster card and the statistics Industries tab's Workplaces column also count the workers who don't count for the worker boost (they walk, drive or haven't come by line in 2 years); the booster card lists them with how they get to work and their home.

params.name: Worker Status
params.tooltip: The booster card's worker list shows what each worker does now (at home, shopping, at work, walking, driving, waiting for or riding a bus, tram, train, ship or aircraft, with the line on hover), where the trip goes, for how many days, the worker's happiness, how far their home town is, and Time Left as a coloured %; the name moves into a tooltip.

params.name: Industry Columns
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab shows plots, each input and output a year without boosts (Recipe In / Out), the boosts on now beside Workload, input, output and shipment per cargo, and each booster's and the worker boost's production increase (green while on); Requirements is left out.

params.name: Statistics Totals
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab counts each cargo once in Input and Output, and Workload compares against the largest recipe.

params.name: Blocked Expansion
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab's Problems column marks industries blocked from further expansion; click the mark to open the industry, which shows what is in the way.

params.name: Cargo Filter
params.tooltip: The statistics Industries tab gets a cargo list next to the eye: it shows only the industries that need, boost with or make the chosen cargo.

params.name: Logging
params.tooltip: Writes the mod's messages to the game log (stdout.txt), for bug reports.
